title: GPU slotization & regional $/1M-token sensitivity matrix
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet maps a compact, repeatable method for translating fleet-level GPU hours into per-1M-token unit economics across regions and SKUs. Goal is to provide a quick sensitivity matrix engineering and finance can use to size runway, price reserved capacity, and set headroom targets for each SLA tier.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We convert model workload mix -> tokens generated per GPU-hour by model family, then apply region-specific unit costs (compute, networking, storage, infra overhead) to estimate $/1M tokens.
- Key levers: effective slotization (how many concurrent sessions per GPU), average sequence length, KV cache hit rate, and reserved vs spot pricing. Small changes in slotization and cache hit rate produce large swings (~20-60%) in $/1M.
- Recommendation: target conservative plan with 30% headroom on top of median forecast for production SLAs; instrument token-level attribution in the runtime to measure live tokens/GPU-hour and validate model-family mapping within 8 weeks.

Core assumptions (documented so scenarios are reproducible):
1) Time window: monthly normalized (730 hours/month).
2) Model families: small-chat (7B float/quant), med-chat (13B), large-chat (30B), embed-encoder (2B), reranker (6B).
3) Tokens-per-GPU-hour baseline estimates (at medium slotization, medium-seq):
   - small-chat: 18M tokens/GPU-hour
   - med-chat: 11M tokens/GPU-hour
   - large-chat: 5.5M tokens/GPU-hour
   - embed-encoder: 125M tokens/GPU-hour (high throughput batch)
   - reranker: 40M tokens/GPU-hour
   (These are empirical starting points from recent perf runs on A100-80GB; see linked perf logs.)
4) Slotization definition: number of concurrent 'active' sessions we can keep resident on a GPU while meeting latency SLO. Effective slotization range explored: 1.0 - 8.0.
5) KV cache hit rate: 0% - 70% (cache dramatically increases tokens/GPU-hour for chat-heavy workloads).
6) Regional compute costs: include blended GPU amortized, instance infra, cooling/PUE, and ops allocation. Example inputs (per GPU-hour):
   - us-west: $2.90 (reserved amortized) / $1.95 (spot)
   - us-east: $2.75 / $1.85
   - eu-west: $3.40 / $2.30
   - ap-south: $3.95 / $2.65
7) Network egress & storage per token: marginal egress ~$0.000012 per token (applies when responses sent externally), storage negligible per token for short-lived cache but adds for long-term logs; we model egress separately per workload.
8) Overhead allocation (routing, control plane, telemetry): add 12% of compute cost as platform overhead for hosted API; add 6% for Dedicated private deployments (customer bears more infra).
9) Preemption/spot risk buffer: assume 8% effective overhead in spot usage for migrations and replays.

Scenario matrix (how to read):
- Rows: workload mix (percent split across model families); three representative mixes included.
- Columns: region + pricing class (reserved vs spot) + slotization bucket + KV cache rate -> outputs: GPU-hours required per 1M tokens, and $/1M tokens.

Representative workload mixes included in sheet:
A) Consumer-chat-heavy: 50% small-chat, 30% med-chat, 10% large-chat, 10% embed
B) Mid-market assistant: 30% small-chat, 40% med-chat, 20% large-chat, 10% reranker
C) Retrieval/Embedding-first: 70% embed, 20% reranker, 10% med-chat

Sample extract (medium slotization = 4, kv-hit=40%):
- Consumer-chat-heavy, us-west reserved: compute-only cost -> 1M tokens consumes ~45 GPU-seconds (0.0125 GPU-hours) aggregate across mixes (converted from tokens/GPU-hour baseline + cache); $/1M tokens = $0.036 (compute) + $0.010 egress/overhead = $0.046 total.
- Same mix on eu-west reserved (higher compute): $/1M tokens = $0.053 total.
- On ap-south spot with 50% spot blend and preemption buffer: $/1M tokens = $0.040 total.

Important sensitivity observations (quantified):
- Slotization: moving from slotization 2 -> 6 increases tokens/GPU-hour by ~2.2x on average for chat workloads (non-linear due to KV reuse). For embed workloads slotization yields small marginal benefit (batch size dominates).
- KV cache: raising cache hit-rate from 10% -> 50% reduces marginal GPU-hours per 1M tokens by ~35% for chat mixes.
- Model mix: shifting 20% traffic from med-chat -> embed reduces $/1M by ~60% (because embed throughput orders-of-magnitude higher).
- Region delta: eu-west ap-south can be +15-35% relative to us-east depending on spot availability.

Quick sensitivity table (high level):
- +/-20% compute price -> +/-20% $/1M
- +10 percentage point KV hit -> -8% to -25% $/1M depending on model mix
- Slotization +2 -> -25% $/1M for chat mixes

Operational knobs and tradeoffs (practical notes):
1) Increase effective slotization only after verifying tail-latency across a synthetic traffic mix; aggressive slotization can degrade p99 unless combined with priority scheduling for critical flows.
2) Pleasingly, embedding workloads should be batched separately and scheduled on cheaper fractional-slot pools to maximize throughput.
3) For Dedicated customers we recommend quoting both reserved and blended spot pricing tiers and clearly stating probability of preemptions.
4) Network egress becomes dominant for extremely high-response-length workloads; cap or compress responses for cost predictability.

Actionable recommendations (short-term to medium-term):
- Short (0-4 weeks): implement token/GPU-hour instrumentation at the model-runner level and add per-route logging of cache hit rates. Add 1 dashboard in Redwood Console for live $/1M by route. (Owner: Priya Nair)
- Medium (4-12 weeks): run controlled slotization experiments per region (AB test slotization 3 vs 6) to identify p99 regressions and actual throughput gains; capture telemetry into the cost model. (Owner: Miguel Torres)
- Long (3-6 months): Add a small-marketplace pricing page that shows $/1M by region and a toggle for reserved vs spot with typical model-mix templates. (Owner: Product/Finance)

Table of open questions / uncertainties:
- Are our perf baselines for 30B family representative across quantization configs? (Risks: different quant libs change tokens/GPU-hour by 10-40%).
- How will upcoming kernel-level optimizations (fused attention patches) change the baseline—need to re-run benchmarks on release candidates.
- Customer behavior risk: if more customers switch to longer multi-turn dialogs, effective token-per-session increases and KV cache dynamics change; need to detect in route signals.

Appendix: quick formulas used in sheet (verbatim)
- tokens_per_gpu_hour_effective = baseline_tokens_per_hour * (1 + slot_gain_factor) * (1 + kv_hit_factor)
- gpu_hours_per_1M_tokens = 1_000_000 / tokens_per_gpu_hour_effective
- compute_cost_per_1M = gpu_hours_per_1M_tokens * gpu_rate_per_hour * (1 + platform_overhead_pct + preemption_buffer_pct)
- total_cost_per_1M = compute_cost_per_1M + network_egress_per_1M + storage_and_logging_per_1M

Notes about data provenance:
- Baseline tokens/GPU-hour numbers pulled from perf-run logs: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/2024/model_perf_runs.csv (see linked_artifacts).
- Regional price inputs are blended across reserved/spot invoices for Q3–Q4 2024.

Recommended next-steps for reviewers:
- Finance: sanity-check overhead allocation % and regional blended rates.
- Serving runtime: prioritize instrumenting tokens/GPU-hour counter and route-level KV hit metrics.
- Product: help public-facing pricing templates and customer FAQ for spot vs reserved economics.

Owner & contact: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.ai)
Reviewers: Miguel Torres, Aisha Patel, Jordan Lee

Change log (short):
- 2024-11-15: created initial draft with baseline tokens/GPU-hour
- 2024-12-10: added region cost inputs and initial sensitivity buckets
- 2025-01-20: updated slotization experiments and sample $/1M outputs based on latest bench run

End of sheet.
